angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 508,557 km at 32.62 pc = 0.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 30.6517 +/- 0.0141 mas (same row, RUWE 1.14): 32.62 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.731 +/- 0.022 solar radii from Osborn et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-431 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.2782O/abstract): 508,557 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.78 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Osborn et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-431 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.2782O/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4850 +/- 75 K from Osborn et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-431 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.2782O/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Osborn et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-431 d in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.2782O/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-431.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.602, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
